assembly_notes:
Identity: one radio enclosure whose front face carries a speaker grille field and a tuning dial, plus a control deck, an optional carry bail and an optional telescoping antenna on the top bay.

core_domain = 4 cabinet_form x 3 grille_style x 2 speaker_layout x 3 control_deck x 3 carry_handle x 3 antenna_module = 648. raw_domain = 648 x 6 control_count values = 3888. Palette, continuous dimensions, rib/bar/hole counts and dial graduations count toward neither.

The previous build of this template failed random-16 with adjacent buttons interpenetrating (button_0/button_1, penetration 6.2 mm) because the keycap row used a fixed x-list that did not grow with the cap size. The rebuild derives control_pitch_m from the selected cap footprint plus 0.006 m of guaranteed air, derives deck_width_m from control_count x control_pitch_m, and then derives cabinet_width_m from deck_width_m. The multiplicity is NOT capped to hide the failure: control_count reaches 8 for every control candidate, including 8 of the largest 0.056 m knobs.

Two host-adaptation rules make every one of the 648 combinations buildable:
(a) top bay. push_button_row mounts on the cabinet top, which the tombstone does not naturally have. The tombstone therefore truncates its arch into a flat crown whose width is exactly the top bay requirement, and its arch rise is re-derived so the front stack still fits under the shoulder. The boombox top bay is cabinet_width_m minus twice its plan corner radius.
(b) front stack. cabinet height drives the speaker field height, not the other way round, so a front-mounted control deck simply pushes the dial and the grille up and the cabinet grows if it must.

No allowance is needed anywhere. Controls pass through real openings cut in the deck plate (ExtrudeWithHoles), the telescoping rod slides inside a real annular bore, and the antenna knuckle is coaxial with its own hinge so raking it sweeps no new volume. ctx.allow_overlap is never called; ctx.allow_isolated_part is never needed because every member touches its host within the 1 mm support band.

Grilles, dial graduations and cabinet trim are welded into single merged meshes so a 40-bar grille costs one collision body, not forty.

derived.expression: selected control cap footprint along the row + 0.006 m
derived.name: control_pitch_m
derived.rationale: Neighbouring caps can only touch if the pitch ignores the cap size, so the pitch is derived from the cap and never from a constant.

derived.expression: control_count * control_pitch_m + 0.020 (+ two knob wells for transport_key_deck)
derived.name: deck_width_m
derived.rationale: The deck footprint is exactly the row it must carry.

derived.expression: max(form nominal width, deck_width_m + 2*front_inset_m + 0.010, top bay requirement)
derived.name: cabinet_width_m
derived.rationale: The host grows for the deck instead of the deck being clipped.

derived.expression: max(form nominal depth, deck_height_m + 0.060 for a top bay, 0.098)
derived.name: cabinet_depth_m
derived.rationale: A top-mounted deck must clear the handle saddle band in Y.

derived.name: deck_plate_thickness_m
derived.rationale: A fully pressed cap must stop inside its own opening rather than diving into the cabinet shell.

derived.expression: single: min(cabinet_width_m - 2*front_inset_m, cabinet_width_m * single_field_width_ratio); dual: (usable width - stereo_field_gap_m)/2
derived.name: field_width_m
derived.rationale: The grille fill must be sized by the opening it fills.

derived.name: field_height_m
derived.rationale: The field takes the height the cabinet leaves after the dial and the front control bay.

derived.expression: ribs: field_height_m / rib_pitch_m; bars: field_width_m / bar_pitch_m; perforations: field footprint / mesh_hole_pitch_m
derived.name: grille_element_count
derived.rationale: Every grille candidate scales its element count with the field it was given rather than reusing a source constant.

derived.expression: cabinet_width_m for the flat-top forms, cabinet_width_m - 2*corner radius for the boombox plan, the flat crown width for the tombstone
derived.name: top_bay_width_m
derived.rationale: Only the genuinely flat part of the top can seat a handle.

derived.name: handle_span_m
derived.rationale: The saddles stay inboard of the antenna socket on every top bay.

derived.name: handle_seat_y_m
derived.rationale: The rear band is reserved for the handle so a top-mounted control deck never shares it.

derived.name: antenna_x_m
derived.rationale: The socket rides the right edge of whatever flat top the form provides, outboard of the handle saddles.

derived.name: antenna_socket_z_m
derived.rationale: The swivel centre sits one knuckle radius above the boss top so the coaxial knuckle only grazes it.

derived.name: antenna_mast_length_m
derived.rationale: The sliding rod must still be captured by the bore at full retraction, whatever stroke was sampled.

multiplicities.host_capacity_expression: deck_width_m = N * control_pitch_m + 0.020 m (plus two flanking knob wells for transport_key_deck); the cabinet then grows so that deck_width_m + 2 * front_inset_m + 0.010 <= cabinet_width_m for a front bay, and deck_width_m + 0.050 <= top_bay_width_m for a top bay
multiplicities.name: control_count
multiplicities.spacing_expression: control_pitch_m = selected cap footprint along the row + 0.006 m of guaranteed air; positions are (i - (N-1)/2) * control_pitch_m

candidates.evidence: Wide softly radiused rectangular cabinet whose front face is set back behind a framed recess and whose top is a finished flat deck.

frame.axis: +Y for the side whip, -X for the rear mast

candidates.name: landscape_cabinet
candidates.notes: One enclosure part is the structural root; the front stack (control bay, tuning dial, speaker field) and the top bay (control bay, handle seat, antenna socket) are derived from what the other slots need.

parameters.rationale: Wide tabletop cabinet width; the reviewed span builds a 0.56 m cabinet.

parameters.name: landscape_height_ratio
parameters.rationale: Height over width of the tabletop cabinet; the source is 0.29/0.56 = 0.52.

candidates.evidence: Perimeter rails enclose a stack of evenly pitched horizontal ribs whose count follows the field height.
candidates.name: horizontal_ribbed
candidates.notes: Emits one welded mesh per speaker field so a dense grille costs one collision body instead of dozens.

parameters.name: rib_pitch_m
parameters.rationale: Vertical spacing of the cloth ribs; the source stacks 15 ribs at 0.0074 m.

candidates.evidence: A dark backing plate, a rounded-rect bezel and a genuinely perforated panel with staggered holes replace the rib stack.
candidates.name: perforated_mesh
candidates.notes: Emits one welded mesh per speaker field so a dense grille costs one collision body instead of dozens.

parameters.name: mesh_hole_pitch_m
parameters.rationale: Perforation pitch; the source panel uses a 0.010 x 0.0086 m staggered grid.

candidates.evidence: The same opening is filled by evenly pitched vertical bars running top to bottom, with the bar count derived from the field width.
candidates.name: vertical_bar
candidates.notes: Emits one welded mesh per speaker field so a dense grille costs one collision body instead of dozens.

parameters.name: bar_pitch_m

candidates.evidence: One circular cone shadow sits behind one wide grille opening that spans most of the front face.
candidates.name: single_field
candidates.notes: Owns how many acoustic fields the front face carries and where they sit; the grille slot only fills them.

parameters.name: single_field_width_ratio
parameters.rationale: Share of the cabinet width taken by the one opening; the source is 0.424/0.56.

candidates.evidence: Two mirrored speaker bores, baskets, surrounds and bezels are emitted at symmetric offsets, halving each opening and freeing the centre.
candidates.name: dual_stereo
candidates.notes: Owns how many acoustic fields the front face carries and where they sit; the grille slot only fills them.

parameters.name: stereo_field_gap_m
parameters.rationale: Clear centre span between the two openings; the source leaves 0.088 m between bore centres.

candidates.evidence: Fluted skirted knob caps seat on the lower control strip and each turns about its own front-facing rotation axis.

dimensions.footprint: control_count x (knob skirt diameter + 0.006) plus 0.010 margins

surface_relation.motion_expression: rotation about the deck normal keeps the knob inside the same opening; there is no travel along the normal
surface_relation.normal_band_expression: the knob body spans -knob_recess (0.0015 m) to knob_height - knob_recess along the outward deck normal, so its skirt is seated but its cap is proud
surface_relation.opening_expression: the deck plate is cut with one round opening of knob skirt diameter + 2 x 0.0008 m per knob, and the knob footprint must stay inside it
surface_relation.required_author_check: category_anchor: every deck control stays inside its opening and proud of the deck

candidates.name: rotary_knob_bank
candidates.notes: A separate deck part is plane-mated onto the cabinet and carries a real opening per control, so no control ever intersects its host.

parameters.name: knob_diameter_m
parameters.rationale: Knob body diameter; the source knob is 0.054 m with a 0.062 m skirt.

candidates.evidence: A darker control strip carries an index-general loop of rounded keycaps, each its own part on a short prismatic press joint.

surface_relation.motion_expression: 0.009 - button_recess - button_travel_m >= 0.0008 m of cap body still protrudes at full press, and the cap never reaches the cabinet shell because the plate is button_recess + button_travel_m + 0.0015 m thick
surface_relation.normal_band_expression: the cap spans -button_recess (0.0020 m) to 0.009 - button_recess along the outward deck normal
surface_relation.opening_expression: the deck plate is cut with one rounded-rect opening of (button_width_m + 0.0016, cap_v + 0.0016) per key; the cap footprint must stay inside it at rest and at full press
surface_relation.required_author_check: category_anchor: every deck control stays inside its opening and proud of the deck

candidates.name: push_button_row
candidates.notes: A separate deck part is plane-mated onto the cabinet and carries a real opening per control, so no control ever intersects its host.

parameters.name: button_width_m
parameters.rationale: Keycap width along the row; the source cap is 0.026 x 0.018 m.

parameters.name: button_travel_m
parameters.rationale: Press stroke; the source prismatic limit is 0.005 m of down travel.

candidates.evidence: Small playback keys press inward from the floor of a recessed tray, flanked by continuously spinning knobs on the same deck.

dimensions.footprint: control_count x (transport_key_width_m + 0.006) plus two flanking knob openings and 0.010 margins

surface_relation.motion_expression: 0.008 - key_recess - transport_key_travel_m >= 0.0008 m of key body is still visible at full press and the key stays in the same opening
surface_relation.normal_band_expression: the key spans -key_recess (0.0025 m) to 0.008 - key_recess along the outward deck normal, which is what makes the tray read as recessed
surface_relation.opening_expression: the recessed deck plate is cut with one rounded-rect opening of (transport_key_width_m + 0.0016, cap_v + 0.0016) per key plus two round knob openings; every key footprint must stay inside its own opening
surface_relation.required_author_check: category_anchor: every deck control stays inside its opening and proud of the deck

candidates.name: transport_key_deck

parameters.name: transport_key_width_m

parameters.name: transport_key_travel_m
parameters.rationale: Key stroke; the source transport joint travels 0.0016 m inward.
